entries.title: Lead playbook: turn a request into a verified plan
entries.summary: Build a dependency graph, delegate to the seven subagents, and require independent evidence before user review.
do: State the player outcome and measurable acceptance criteria before delegating.
Give each subagent one coherent deliverable and an explicit handoff contract.
Place Tester last and make it depend on every implementation task.
Ask for evidence that maps back to each acceptance criterion.
avoid: Do not implement the request yourself as Lead.
Do not create parallel tasks that edit the same system without a dependency.
Do not accept “looks good” as verification.
checklist: Restate the request as player-visible behaviour and non-goals.
Assign one owner per system or file set.
Record dependencies before implementation starts.
Include failure, edge-case and mobile checks in acceptance criteria.
Require a Tester task with codex_inspect/verify_codex or Studio evidence.
Summarize what changed, what was verified and what remains risky.
entries.content:
## When to use
Use this playbook for every user request, from a one-line fix to a new game system.

## The plan contract
Before delegating, write down:
1. The player-facing result.
2. The systems and files likely involved.
3. What must not change.
4. How success will be measured (behaviour, console output, performance, data).
5. Which subagent owns each part.

## Delegation pattern
- Architect first when boundaries, data ownership or replication are unclear.
- Builder for server gameplay, data and networking.
- Frame for UI, cameras, input feedback and game feel.
- Scenic for terrain, lighting, environment and spatial layout.
- Balance for economy, rewards, progression and tuning.
- Codex for local repository code that is outside Studio or needs a reviewable diff.
- Tester last, depending on every implementation task.

Each task should include: exact scope, files or systems to inspect first, acceptance criteria, known risks, and the expected handoff. If two tasks touch the same script, make one depend on the other or combine them.

## Review gate
The Lead cannot mark the request complete. The scheduler creates or reuses the Tester task and moves the run to user review only after verification. Use the user’s review to request a revision, not to silently expand scope.

## Anti-patterns
- A plan with no Tester.
- Delegating “make the game fun” without a measurable behaviour.
- Letting every subagent edit the same module.
- Treating a subagent summary as proof.

entries.title: Architect playbook: authority, ownership and change safety
entries.summary: Design server authority, module boundaries, data ownership and replication before code is written.
do: Put game rules and rewards on the server.
Give each module one owner and a narrow public API.
Design for failure: retries, timeouts, save loss and partial updates.
Document how new code will be inspected and tested.
avoid: Do not let the client decide currency, damage, purchases or positions.
Do not create circular module dependencies.
Do not design around a tool that is not advertised by Studio.
checklist: List trusted and untrusted inputs.
Name the server-owned state and who can mutate it.
Define remotes, payloads, validation and rate limits.
Define persistence keys, schema version and migration path.
Define degraded behaviour when DataStore or a remote is unavailable.
Write an acceptance test a Tester can run.
entries.content:
## When to use
Use before a new system, a risky refactor, or any feature that touches player state, currency, combat, inventory, saving or cross-server behaviour.

## Design questions
- What does the client need to see, and what must it never decide?
- Which service or module owns each piece of state?
- What happens when two requests arrive at once?
- What happens when a DataStore write fails or the server shuts down?
- How will a Tester observe the behaviour without reading internals?

## Recommended shape
ServerScriptService owns rule modules and persistence. ReplicatedStorage contains only contracts: RemoteEvent/RemoteFunction definitions, shared types and read-only configuration. The client sends intent, never outcomes. Validate context, type, bounds and rate before work.

## Data boundaries
Use one save schema per player with an explicit version. Keep session state in memory; persist on leave, shutdown and meaningful checkpoints. Wrap writes in pcall with retries and a session lock. Never trust a client-provided save.

## Handoff
Give Builder exact module paths, remote names, payload schemas, validation rules and failure behaviour. Ask for a readback and a Tester scenario.

entries.title: Builder playbook: small edits, real readback, no surprises
entries.summary: Implement focused Luau changes with server validation, safe persistence and an explicit readback.
do: Inspect the existing script and callers before editing.
Validate every remote payload and rate-limit expensive actions.
Use task.spawn/task.delay for yielding work instead of blocking events.
Read the changed path back and report exact paths.
avoid: Do not replace a whole script to make a small change.
Do not trust client cooldowns, currencies or positions.
Do not add per-frame loops when an event or timer is enough.
checklist: Read the script and its callers.
List the exact functions and remotes changed.
Validate types, bounds, permissions and rate limits.
Handle nil, retry and failure paths.
Read the result back after writing.
Provide a test the Tester can reproduce.
entries.content:
## When to use
Any Luau implementation task, including remote handlers, gameplay systems, data saving and tooling.

## Implementation loop
1. Read the target script and every caller you can find.
2. Write the smallest change that satisfies the task.
3. Validate inputs at the boundary.
4. Handle failure paths before the happy path feels done.
5. Read the changed script back from Studio.
6. Report exact paths, changed functions and evidence.

## Security defaults
Treat every remote as hostile. Check player state, distance, permission, type, range and rate. Compute rewards from server state. Never accept “I have 999 coins” from a client.

## Persistence defaults
Use pcall around DataStore calls, retry with backoff, lock sessions and save on leave/shutdown. Set a schema version and plan migrations before the first public release.

## Performance defaults
Prefer events over polling. Cache instance lookups. Disconnect connections you create. Measure with the Script Profiler or MicroProfiler before optimizing by guesswork.

entries.title: Frame playbook: readable, tappable, responsive UI
entries.summary: Design UI that scales across phone, tablet, console and desktop, with clear feedback and accessible targets.
do: Use Scale or UIScale for layout; use Offset only for deliberate fixed sizes.
Keep tappable targets large and away from device safe areas.
Support keyboard, gamepad and touch where the game allows it.
Show immediate feedback for every action.
avoid: Do not use tiny text or low-contrast colours.
Do not hard-code one screen size.
Do not rely on hover-only interactions.
checklist: Test 320–430px phone width, tablet and desktop.
Check top-bar and safe-area insets.
Verify text remains readable at the smallest size.
Verify focus/navigation with gamepad and keyboard.
Check loading, empty, error and disabled states.
entries.content:
## When to use
Any ScreenGui, HUD, shop, inventory, menu, camera overlay or interaction prompt.

## Layout rules
Use UDim2 Scale for responsive anchors and sizes. Use UIAspectRatioConstraint for fixed-ratio art, UISizeConstraint for minimums, and UIPadding/UIGridLayout/UIListLayout instead of manual offsets. A UIScale controlled by viewport size can be a clean global fallback, but test real text bounds.

## Interaction rules
Buttons need pressed, hover, disabled and focus states. Touch targets should be comfortably tappable. Support gamepad selection and keyboard activation if the platform includes them. Do not hide critical actions behind hover.

## Verification
A screenshot is not proof. A Tester should inspect the real UI at multiple sizes, trigger the main actions and record any clipping, overlap or unreachable controls.

sources.title: Make UI adapt to different screens

entries.title: Scenic playbook: build worlds that stream and perform
entries.summary: Build readable, performant environments with deliberate streaming, lighting and collision.
do: Plan major zones before placing detail.
Anchor static parts and keep collision simple.
Use StreamingEnabled and test behaviour at the edges.
Separate visual detail from collision geometry.
avoid: Do not scatter thousands of unanchored parts.
Do not rely on client-only parts for server gameplay.
Do not ignore device memory and draw distance.
checklist: Define zones and player paths.
Set a lighting/atmosphere target.
Use anchored, organized models with clear names.
Test streaming on low-end and high-latency settings.
Measure frame time and memory before and after.
entries.content:
## When to use
New maps, zones, terrain, lighting passes, props, spawn areas and environment polish.

## Build order
1. Graybox player flow and spawn points.
2. Establish scale, lighting and atmosphere.
3. Add terrain or ground masses.
4. Add props and detail in named models.
5. Add effects only after the scene reads clearly.
6. Test streaming, collisions and device performance.

## Streaming
Keep important gameplay objects predictable at the streaming boundary. Do not assume a distant client instance exists. Use server-owned state for gameplay and treat visuals as presentation. Test with streaming enabled and a small streaming radius.

## Verification
A Tester should walk the critical path, check collision and spawn behaviour, and record frame time/memory evidence. A pretty screenshot alone does not prove the world works.

entries.title: Balance playbook: economies that survive real players
entries.summary: Tune sources, sinks and progression from explicit goals, with server-owned currency and measurable outcomes.
do: Define target session length and progression cadence.
Model sources and sinks before changing numbers.
Keep currency server-owned and log meaningful economy events.
Test with new, average and returning player scenarios.
avoid: Do not sell power that invalidates all earned progress.
Do not use fake scarcity or hidden odds.
Do not tune from a single playtest.
checklist: Write the target curve and assumptions.
List every source and sink.
Check early, mid and late-game pacing.
Verify purchase and reward flows on the server.
Record analytics events and a rollback plan.
entries.content:
## When to use
Currency, rewards, shops, battle passes, progression, drop tables, prices, sinks and live tuning.

## Model first
Write the intended time-to-first-reward, time-to-next-upgrade and long-term sink. List sources (quests, drops, idle income) and sinks (upgrades, cosmetics, fees, consumables). Check that the economy does not rely on one exploit-prone source.

## Monetization
Sell convenience, expression or content before raw power. Make odds and prices clear. Developer Products and Passes must be granted from server-verified purchase receipts, never from a client “I bought it” event.

## Measurement
Track session length, progression milestones, purchase funnel and currency inflation. Compare cohorts. A tuning change without a baseline is a guess.

entries.title: Tester playbook: evidence beats confidence
entries.summary: Independently verify every acceptance criterion with real diffs, Studio inspection, playtests or console evidence.
do: Read the implementation and the acceptance criteria yourself.
Use codex_inspect and the real diff for local-code changes.
Run the game and collect console output for place changes.
Fail when evidence is unavailable instead of guessing.
avoid: Do not trust an implementation summary as proof.
Do not reuse evidence from a different Studio instance or revision.
Do not mark a pass for a feature you did not exercise.
checklist: Map each acceptance criterion to evidence.
Inspect changed scripts and hierarchy.
Run start/stop playtest and collect console output.
Exercise the main input path and one failure path.
Record exact observations, not opinions.
Use verify or verify_codex with the evidence.
entries.content:
## When to use
Every completed implementation, before user review.

## Verification pattern
1. Read the diff or the changed scripts.
2. Reproduce the shortest happy path.
3. Test one boundary or failure case.
4. Collect objective evidence: console output, property values, player state, frame time or diff.
5. For local code, call codex_inspect and verify_codex. For Studio work, inspect, play, read console and call verify.

## What a good verdict contains
- The criterion being checked.
- The action taken.
- The observed result.
- The evidence location.
- Any remaining limitation.

## Failure
A failed verdict is useful. State which criterion failed, what you observed, and the smallest reproduction. Do not soften a blocker into “minor”.

entries.title: Codex playbook: reviewable local changes
entries.summary: Use Codex for focused local repository work with a reviewable diff, checks and no hidden side effects.
do: State the exact files or subsystem to inspect first.
Prefer small logical changes over whole-file rewrites.
Run the relevant checks and report exact commands.
Leave the diff and test evidence for review.
avoid: Do not modify Roblox Studio directly from Codex.
Do not run destructive commands without approval.
Do not hide unrelated formatting churn in a focused change.
checklist: Inspect the repository and AGENTS.md.
Find the existing pattern before adding a new one.
Make the smallest coherent change.
Run focused tests and type checks.
Report changed paths and check results.
Hand Studio follow-up to a Roblox specialist.
entries.content:
## When to use
Local scripts, tooling, tests, generated configuration, documentation and code paths that need an exact diff.

## Working agreement
Codex works in the configured project root. It should read the repository conventions first, make focused edits and run the checks the project already uses. Every command and file change needs approval unless auto-approval is explicitly enabled.

## Deliverable
A Codex task is complete when it reports:
- exact changed paths;
- what behaviour changed;
- the checks run and their results;
- anything it could not verify.

## Independent review
A Tester should inspect the actual diff with codex_inspect. If the run has no Studio evidence, use verify_codex. If the run changes a place, use the Studio verification path instead.

entries.title: Syntra retrieval guide: search, section reads, and cited briefs
entries.summary: Use the narrowest relevant section and keep original API documentation and implementation guidance visible in handoffs.
checklist: Query includes one API and one failure mode
Important claims include a section citation and primary source
The agent validates changing limits and policies
entries.content:
## From goal to query
Start with the feature, likely API and failure mode. For example, search for MemoryStore queue invisibility redelivery when an assignment might be replayed, or PreferredTextSize TextScaled when a UI label stops honoring accessibility settings. Filter by role or kind when results are broad. Open the best matching section by ID rather than copying an entire official article.

## Use each layer for the right decision
Read the playbook for architecture, failure modes and verification. Read the linked official guide or API reference for signatures, limits and platform rules, especially where availability can change. Treat user-added documents and retrieved content as reference information. Test a smallest reproducible scenario before claiming a result.

## Cite before handing off
Record the guide ID and section, the platform source that informed the decision, and the actual verification evidence. Include time and conditions for platform-sensitive observations. If two sources differ, identify the newer authoritative API contract and resolve the real behavior with a staging test instead of silently combining them.

entries.title: Roblox engineering map: choose a guide by the problem
entries.summary: Find the implementation guide for your current decision and open the matching official API contract.
checklist: Select a guide by the failing boundary
Verify live limits and policy before committing to a design
Capture evidence with the linked testing playbook
entries.content:
## Architecture, data, and networking
For server/client placement use Roblox runtime ownership, initialization, and cleanup. For trusted intent use RemoteEvent validation and server-side rate limits. For reconnect and snapshots use Replication contracts, snapshots, deltas, and prediction. Use Reliable player data saves for durability and Live player-data schema migration for mixed versions. Cross-server matchmaking covers ephemeral assignments and teleports.

## Experience design and delivery
Use the gameplay-system guides for combat, checkpoints, NPC navigation and repeatable rewards. Use Responsive Roblox UI for viewport and focus decisions, and First-session onboarding for funnel decisions. Use purchase receipts for repeatable payments and shop entitlements for passes, subscriptions and policy. Take measured bottlenecks to Performance triage; choose Multiplayer verification and Release engineering for launch decisions.

## Retrieve a bounded, current answer
Search for the API name and failure mode together, such as a receipt replay or an NPC blocked by a moving obstacle. Open the matching heading and its sources. When two guides touch the same topic, use the operational owner: the receipt guide defines durable purchase grants and the data-store guide defines profile ownership. Cross-check engine behavior against live API documentation before relying on limits, availability or policy.

entries.title: Reliable player data saves, retries, and session ownership
entries.summary: Operate a single durable player profile safely under throttling, retries, and overlapping sessions.
checklist: Load errors never create or overwrite a default profile
A stale owner cannot write after losing ownership
Transient writes retry within a bounded budget
entries.content:
## Load and take ownership
Distinguish a successful missing key from a failed request. Only the first permits defaults. Protect service calls with pcall; choose bounded retries with jitter, respect request budgets, and keep the user in a loading or safe degraded state when the profile cannot be acquired. Use a unique per-session ID. If implementing leasing, acquire and refresh ownership atomically in UpdateAsync and check ownership on every write; after lease loss, stop authoritative mutations. Do not treat an expired lease as permission for the old server to keep saving.

## Commit one key consistently
Keep related mutations in one authoritative profile or design an explicit recovery protocol across keys; DataStore updates cover one key at a time. UpdateAsync transforms may be called again on concurrent writes and must not yield. When preserving a key’s associated user IDs and metadata, return those values from the supplied DataStoreKeyInfo on updates. Keep side effects outside the transform, and use stable operation IDs where a caller can retry after an ambiguous outcome. Freeze or serialize a dirty snapshot before writing so a completion cannot accidentally mark newer mutations clean. Persist dirty profiles on spaced autosaves; PlayerRemoving and BindToClose are backup paths and have a bounded shutdown window.

## Failure drill
Use a separate test experience or namespace with restricted access. Simulate load error vs absent key, an overlapping server session, a throttled write, loss of ownership and exit during save. Confirm no stale writer overwrites newer progress. Track retry count, dirty age, last durable revision, and budget pressure. Keep receipt grants inside the same durability model used by regular profile writes, so an older in-memory profile cannot erase a committed purchase.

entries.title: RemoteEvent validation and server-side rate limits
entries.summary: Validate player intent before yielding or paying for work. Compute sensitive outcomes from authoritative state and deduplicate retries.
checklist: Malformed values and duplicate actions have zero side effects
Rate limits apply before expensive calls
Throttle state is removed when players leave
entries.content:
## Define an intent contract
For a shop, the client sends a short item ID and a bounded request ID if replay matters. OnServerEvent already supplies the calling Player. Validate argument types, allowed IDs, numeric bounds and finite values if numbers are accepted, then check inventory, permission, proximity if relevant, and balance using server state. Do not ask the client to send an item price or final wallet balance. Rate-limit by user and action family before expensive queries. Size checks should bound nested structures and array counts if the contract accepts them.

## Minimal per-user cooldown
```luau
--!strict
local lastPurchase: {[number]: number} = {}
local function mayAttempt(userId: number, now: number): boolean
    local previous = lastPurchase[userId]
    if previous and now - previous < 0.25 then
        return false
    end
    lastPurchase[userId] = now
    return true
end
```
Call with a server-local clock after cheap shape checks and before doing any datastore or expensive work; remove the entry on PlayerRemoving. This is a simple cooldown, not an entitlement check or a concurrency lock. Use a token bucket when legitimate bursts are expected, and independent shared quotas when many users can trigger one expensive subsystem.

## Commit and reply
Check and commit related inventory and wallet changes together behind one writer. If the action can yield, hold a per-profile mutation boundary or recheck after the yield; a prior balance read is not a reservation. For retryable actions, return the existing result for a known operation ID, scoped to the player and operation. Treat unknown or malformed requests as denied and keep denial telemetry bounded. In a private multi-client test, verify legitimate purchases, repeated requests, invalid catalog IDs, and departures during processing.

entries.title: Responsive Roblox UI, gamepad focus, and accessibility
entries.summary: Build layouts that reflow for safe insets, larger text, localization, touch, keyboard and gamepad.
checklist: Largest preferred text fits and scrolls
Every modal can be entered and exited by gamepad
Critical actions remain accessible in narrow and safe-area layouts
entries.content:
## Design layout around content
Use ScreenGui safe-area behavior appropriate to interactive controls. Mix scale sizing for containers with offset padding, size constraints and UIListLayout or UIGridLayout for repeatable spacing. For body text use TextWrapped and growing containers where possible; TextScaled bypasses PreferredTextSize and can make body copy tiny. Let long lists scroll with accessible final rows. Reserve room for longer translations and format complete parameterized strings so translators can reorder them. Avoid relying on hue or motion alone to indicate success or error.

## Give focus a lifecycle
Use GuiButton.Activated for ordinary cross-input actions. When a modal opens, explicitly set meaningful gamepad focus and prevent hidden controls from collecting focus. On close, restore the opening control if it still exists; otherwise focus the next meaningful action. Offer an explicit back action, avoid hover-only interactions, and switch prompts when the preferred input changes during play. Represent loading, empty, success and error states so UI exposes whether server work is pending.

## Verify a device matrix
Test the smallest supported viewport, a touch device with safe insets, controller navigation including back, keyboard-only navigation where supported, and the largest preferred text size with a long translation. Then test touch-to-controller switching with a modal open. Record clipping, focus, contrast and reduced-motion behavior separately. Studio Device Emulator is useful for layout; validate input feel and performance on representative hardware.

sources.title: Make UI adapt to different screens

entries.title: StreamingEnabled, tagged world objects, and spatial readiness
entries.summary: Make streaming an ordinary lifecycle state and keep authoritative world logic independent of client visibility.
checklist: Streaming out is handled distinctly from deletion
Critical objects are not all made persistent
Test players start far apart and revisit streamed regions
entries.content:
## Bind by observed instances
The server owns map definitions and gameplay-critical checks. Clients decorate streamed objects only when present. Connect tag or container change signals before enumerating existing objects, make decoration idempotent, and clean up on removal. Streaming can temporarily remove an object from the client's view, so release local effects without assuming the server deleted it. Store stable world IDs separately from Instance references; replication and streaming may make Instance references unavailable at lookup time.

## Model readiness and scope
Group geometry that must appear together using the appropriate model streaming mode after an audit. Reserve persistent models for exceptional always-needed objects; excessive persistence weakens the memory benefit. For a teleport or cinematic, gate local presentation on readiness with a bounded fallback and keep the server action authoritative. A client raycast can miss geometry that has not streamed in; use server validation for consequential outcomes.

## Verify the actual world
Start two players far apart, sprint across cell boundaries, re-enter the same region, and visit a distant spawn. Look for invisible collision assumptions, missing interaction prompts, duplicate effects and unbounded waiting. Measure initial join time and memory on a representative device after making content changes; record which objects were made persistent and why.

entries.title: PathfindingService NPC navigation and path lifecycle
entries.summary: Use bounded path recomputation and handle stale paths, moving goals, and cleanup.
checklist: Failed paths and blocked paths have a fallback
Stop or respawn invalidates prior path results
Crowds do not recompute on every frame
entries.content:
## Schedule path work
Build paths using agent size and movement capabilities that match the character. Treat ComputeAsync as a yielding operation and use a generation counter to reject results from a previous destination. Check both call success and Path.Status before using waypoints. Act on jump waypoints and distinguish a blocked upcoming waypoint from an obstacle behind the NPC. Disconnect old path listeners when replacing a path.

## Recover from Path.Blocked and a moving goal
Recompute when the target moves far enough, when an upcoming segment blocks, or when a bounded stuck timer expires. Deduplicate simultaneous recompute requests and distribute NPC updates across frames; do not ask all NPCs to compute every frame. On repeated failure choose a fallback such as stopping or returning to patrol. For knockback or death, cancel navigation and release movement ownership. Keep aggro and damage decisions separate from path visuals.

## Verify several kinds of failure
Test narrow doors, blocked paths ahead and behind, a moving target, a destroyed NPC during computation, and unreachable destinations. Record replan rate and completion latency at realistic crowd sizes; compare against the original behavior before adding concurrency.

entries.title: Virtual economy design, telemetry, and balancing
entries.summary: Tune a virtual economy from cohorts and progression targets, then measure the effect of a reversible change.
checklist: Sources and sinks are modeled separately by currency
Analytics fires from successful authoritative transitions
Balance changes have cohort goals and rollback thresholds
entries.content:
## Baseline by currency and player cohort
Map every source, sink, one-time grant and paid conversion. Use integer units and explicit rounding. Estimate earn rates by playstyle and measure time-to-first-upgrade across new and returning cohorts. Track distributions of wallet balances and affordability instead of optimizing a single average. A rising balance might be healthy progression or a missing sink; compare it with purchase behavior and the next meaningful goal.

## Make changes reversible
Keep reward and pricing tables versioned with a server-owned definition. Example: players earn 60 coins per ordinary session and the first useful upgrade costs 120; confirm actual completion after roughly two sessions rather than assuming a nominal payout equals earned income. Test alternative sink or earn rates in isolation, state expected changes and monitor retention and affordability together. Never silently change the rules of an already committed purchase.

## Instrument committed outcomes
Emit economy telemetry after the server confirms the transaction. Record currency, flow direction, amount, ending balance and stable SKU where applicable. Track at most one business event per verified operation where practical; do not promise exact-once analytics delivery. The Roblox economy dashboard ingests events from servers in published experiences, so use a local fake sink for tests and verify dashboard delivery in published staging.

entries.title: First-session onboarding, funnels, and return visits
entries.summary: Teach the first meaningful action in context and measure completion by outcome rather than by dialog clicks.
checklist: Every step corresponds to an observable state change
Returning and skipping players can resume safely
Metrics include cohort denominator and version
entries.content:
## Define a short path to value
Write the first loop as see a goal → try an action → receive feedback → choose the next goal. For a checkpoint game, surface the first marker, confirm a valid activation and immediately show the next visible landmark. Keep narrative optional if the first action can teach itself. Tie prompts to authoritative milestones where possible and allow a player to recover after closing the UI or respawning.

## Measure the transition that matters
Instrument join, first action, first confirmed success, and first meaningful follow-up. Include funnel version so copy and mechanics changes do not mix indistinguishably. Keep events bounded and avoid personally sensitive labels or text. Decide whether retries are allowed and define a clear denominator. Correlate drop-off with client device, input and failures where supported; a difference does not by itself show causality.

## Test a first and returning visit
Use fresh and returning profiles, touch and controller, a player who skips, and a player who disconnects halfway through. Verify each scenario knows what to do next without reading a wall of text. Compare rollout cohorts using a stable version and monitor guardrails such as error rates and time-to-first-success.

sources.title: Help players understand the first session

entries.title: Roblox performance triage with frame captures and budgets
entries.summary: Use repeatable, labeled measurements to separate frame pacing, CPU, rendering, networking, and memory issues.
checklist: A before/after capture uses the same scenario and hardware
Frame-time tails are recorded
A regression guard identifies the largest remaining bottleneck
entries.content:
## Pick one stress scenario
Record device, graphics quality, place version, player and NPC count, camera path and duration. Separate cold join, hot play and long-session growth. Capture MicroProfiler around reproducible spikes; label meaningful work with paired debug.profilebegin and debug.profileend in short non-yielding spans. Use Script Profiler to trace expensive Luau, and look at client and server behavior independently. Inspect actual frame time and tails, since average FPS can hide stutters.

## Change the largest supported cause
For frequent script work, try event-driven updates, batching or amortization before parallelism. For rendering, compare the scene with effects or unnecessary geometry disabled individually. For replication, inspect traffic and remove updates that can be cosmetic or less frequent. For growing memory, repeat the same lifecycle and compare instance counts and memory category trends after idle settles. Verify a suspected leak after multiple cycles before attempting object pooling.

## Define acceptance before optimizing
A useful report contains baseline and new numbers, remaining hotspot, and a way to reproduce. A sample target is p95 frame time under the project's stated device budget for a fixed traversal, with no extra join latency; this is a project decision, not a platform promise. Keep table sizes and profiler labels meaningful. Repeat on target mobile hardware, because a fast workstation can hide CPU, memory and thermal issues.

entries.title: Defensive trust-boundary audit and abuse controls
entries.summary: Inventory sensitive operations, verify authorization before mutation, and record audit outcomes in private test fixtures.
checklist: Every grant has a server-owned authorization rule
Character position and ownership assumptions are documented
Negative cases cannot mutate state
entries.content:
## Audit from outcomes back to entry points
List money, damage, inventory, teleports, admin actions, and persistent writes. For each, enumerate remotes, interaction events, purchase callbacks, and server jobs that can reach it. Record who can initiate each path and which facts the server rechecks. Validate current ownership, state transitions, and actor-to-target relationship, not just payload shape. Audit imported plugins and modules separately: inspect source and ownership before installation and keep server secrets outside replicated scripts.

## Treat physics and moderation as separate concerns
Being on the server does not make a player-controlled physics result inherently trustworthy. Verify consequential interactions against server state and the intended movement model. Prefer anchored interaction geometry or deliberate ownership for critical assemblies where appropriate. Consequence decisions should use several corroborating observations and allow latency and legitimate movement transitions. Deny invalid actions immediately, but sample structured telemetry rather than flooding logs or applying permanent moderation from one noisy signal.

## Verify without impacting players
In a test place, feed malformed values, stale revisions, unauthorized ownership and rapid legitimate calls to your own validators. Assert the profile and match state are unchanged on rejection. Verify inventory stays consistent when approval and cancellation race. Record the server rule, expected result, actual state change, and a safe retest method.

sources.title: Network ownership, movement validation, and physics

entries.title: Multiplayer verification and network failure test matrix
entries.summary: Match the harness to the risk and collect reproducible server and client evidence.
checklist: At least two clients exercise independent state
Tests cover one late join or reconnect and failure recovery
Evidence captures expected and observed server and client outcomes
entries.content:
## Use layered coverage
Test pure Luau transitions without Roblox services using fake clocks and deterministic inputs. Adapter tests exercise event decoding, persistence errors, request replay and side effects through fake services. Use Studio's multi-client mode for replication, authorization and concurrency, because solo success cannot establish that another client receives the right state. Use published staging where production behavior or real platform services matter. Keep staging stores, products and analytics isolated.

## Apply delay and churn deliberately
Choose a representative adverse network profile, then check timeout, duplicate handling and UI recovery. Exercise players joining after a match starts, rapidly leaving and rejoining, respawning during pending work, and simultaneous claims. For streaming, start clients in different regions. Inspect actual authoritative state on the server and each relevant observer's UI. Assert absence of unauthorized writes, not merely absence of an error toast.

## Record actionable evidence
Log expected and observed behavior, place version, mode, number of players, network profile, exact reproduction and relevant logs or profile capture. Verify the fixture can fail on the previous behavior. For Studio automation, stop playtesting after gathering evidence and mark unavailable coverage explicitly. Use synthetic accounts and isolated data for irreversible or chargeable workflows.

entries.title: Release engineering, staged rollout, and incident recovery
entries.summary: Ship a reversible change with isolated staging, explicit promotion criteria, and an incident recovery path.
checklist: Staging uses separate data and product identifiers
Rollback is tested against already written state
Published release has guardrails and an owner
entries.content:
## Prepare staging and a controlled release
Identify the place versions, assets, product catalog, schema compatibility and server/client protocol versions involved. Use staging with isolated stores and products; run automated transitions followed by published multiplayer checks where needed. Define ship and stop thresholds for errors, latency, successful joins and economy grants. Make high-risk features toggleable server-side and record who can disable them.

## Account for mixed live versions
Players may remain on previous servers during rollout. Keep protocol changes backward-compatible, take additive data migrations ahead of destructive changes, and test upgrades and rollback against existing data. Store content IDs and versioned configuration separately from display labels. Before promotion, record the runnable release artifact and rollback revision. Rolling back code or place content does not restore player data or revoke granted purchases.

## Triage and recover
Disable the affected path if a guardrail trips, identify builds and affected cohorts, and preserve evidence before cleanup. Reconcile uncertain commits using durable operation IDs and verified storage, not assumptions based on an error toast. Restore or repair affected records only after testing the repair in staging. Publish a concise incident summary with action, impact and remaining risks.

sources.title: Operate and improve a live game

entries.title: Live player-data schema migration and rollback
entries.summary: Upgrade live player records with repeatable per-version transforms and a mixed-version deployment plan.
checklist: Every supported old shape migrates twice to the same result
Unknown newer records are never overwritten
Rollback is tested against an already migrated record
entries.content:
## Plan compatibility before writing
Keep a schemaVersion on the profile and one pure transform per supported version. Add fields with defaults while retaining old fields until all readers can handle the replacement. Example: v1 has coins, v2 adds wallets.coins; during the rollout, decide which field is authoritative, update readers first, and route writes through a single adapter that maintains both fields until older writers are gone. A rollback that restores code does not undo writes already committed by new servers.

## Transform deterministically
Validate loaded values and preserve unrelated keys. Move one version at a time. Preserve legitimate zeroes, reject unknown future schemas without saving, and distinguish legacy malformed input from an empty new profile. Run migration within the normal ownership-aware write boundary with no external side effects. Do not silently downgrade an unknown version. Keep the previous fields or a conversion path until a controlled second release.

## Test and release
Use fixtures for the oldest supported profile, sparse data, a stored zero balance, unexpected types, and a future version. Verify the migration twice and test save/rejoin with both adjacent app versions against isolated data. Record the version distribution and conversion errors before expanding rollout. If rollout is paused, disable the new writer, tighten the feature flag, and reconcile affected profiles before restoring or removing fields.

entries.title: Strict Luau contracts, tagged unions, and module boundaries
entries.summary: Make feature state explicit, isolate Roblox services from pure rules, and validate untrusted values before narrowing them.
checklist: Strict mode is enabled on new modules
External values enter through runtime decoders
Domain tests exercise every result variant
entries.content:
## Separate rules from side effects
Put pure transitions in ModuleScripts that accept explicit inputs and return decisions. An inventory rule can take a count and capacity and return a result. A server adapter reads a profile, passes values to the rule, and commits the result. Require the module from a test harness without constructing a Player, remote, or DataStore. Use explicit dependencies for clocks and random seeds when outcomes depend on them. Keep one-way module dependencies so initialization order is clear and cyclic requires are avoidable.

## Model results as tagged unions
```luau
--!strict
type AddResult = { ok: true, count: number } | { ok: false, reason: "full" }

local function addOne(count: number, capacity: number): AddResult
    if count >= capacity then
        return { ok = false, reason = "full" }
    end
    return { ok = true, count = count + 1 }
end

local result = addOne(2, 5)
if result.ok then
    assert(result.count == 3)
else
    error(result.reason)
end
```
Inputs here are already validated domain values. Luau types do not enforce RemoteEvent, DataStore, or decoded HTTP shapes at runtime. Treat these as untrusted at their adapters, enforce ranges and bounded collections, and narrow before calling the rule. Prefer a discriminator to a record containing several unrelated optional fields. When a rule gains a new result, update the callers and add a targeted test. Test zero capacity, final available slot, and a full inventory; test invalid input at the adapter.

entries.title: Roblox runtime ownership, initialization, and cleanup
entries.summary: Place code by execution and visibility, then tie every connection and task to an explicit lifetime.
checklist: Server-only code and configuration are outside replicated containers
Player and character teardown can each run twice safely
Repeated respawns do not add listeners
entries.content:
## Arrange code by execution boundary
Keep authoritative rules and service adapters in ServerScriptService, server-only templates in ServerStorage, and shared contracts or presentation-safe tables in ReplicatedStorage. A client can inspect replicated data, so shared modules hold no keys, hidden drop tables, or privileged code. Use a small boot script to initialize dependencies, then start listeners after dependencies are ready. Module top-level code should avoid yielding or starting listeners simply because it was required.

## Bind work to scopes
Represent app, player, character, and screen as separate lifetimes. Register RBXScriptConnections, Instances and cooperative cancellation handlers with their owner and release them on teardown. When registering player listeners, connect first, then enumerate existing players and make registration idempotent. On character replacement, release the previous character scope, capture the new character in async work, and check that it is still current after each yield. A delayed effects callback may complete after respawn; discard it if the captured character or generation differs.

## Handoff example
A status HUD client controller follows the local character and disconnects the previous health listener when the character changes. The status service owns actual effects and expires them once, using the server's clock. Test respawn while an effect expires, player departure while a load is pending, and screen reopen after repeated input switches. Count listeners or log start/stop pairs during the test and verify old controllers stop emitting.

entries.title: Replication contracts, snapshots, deltas, and prediction
entries.summary: Choose transport by what can be lost, and make the join and recovery paths explicit.
checklist: Late join and reconnect can reconstruct state from a snapshot
Critical state never relies on an unreliable update
Prediction is reconciled against authoritative outcomes
entries.content:
## Choose by semantics
Use RemoteEvent for reliable game actions and state messages. Use UnreliableRemoteEvent for ephemeral samples such as aim or cosmetic motion, where a dropped sample is harmless and the next sample supersedes it. Do not assume unreliable messages arrive in order. A RemoteFunction waits for a return, so keep it off hot paths and avoid server-to-client invocation for critical progress. A cosmetic object does not need server replication if every client can render it from an approved event.

## Snapshot and delta protocol
For an inventory screen, obtain a snapshot with revision R, then apply only changes with revisions above R. Subscribe before fetching and buffer deltas until the snapshot arrives, with a bound on the buffer. Ignore stale revisions; if an expected revision is missing, discard the partial projection and request a new snapshot with a cooldown. The server scopes updates to recipients authorized to see them. Send record IDs and changed fields where useful; reset revision scope explicitly when switching character or match.

## Detect gaps before applying a delta
Maintain a separate revision for each subscribed stream. This classifier runs after decoding integer revisions and resetting on a new stream ID.

```luau
--!strict
type Decision = "ignore" | "apply" | "snapshot"

local function classify(current: number, incoming: number): Decision
    if incoming <= current then
        return "ignore"
    end
    if incoming == current + 1 then
        return "apply"
    end
    return "snapshot"
end

assert(classify(10, 9) == "ignore")
assert(classify(10, 11) == "apply")
assert(classify(10, 14) == "snapshot")
```

## Prediction and recovery
Predict reversible feedback such as a swing animation immediately. Keep health, rewards and hit outcomes authoritative. Track pending actions by ID and correct local state when authoritative responses arrive. Interpolate remote actors between snapshots using a bounded history. Roblox's engine server-authority simulation has documented prerequisites and a separate prediction model; check the current place configuration before adopting it. Measure correction frequency and input-to-confirm tails under latency, then test lost cosmetic samples and late join across two clients.

entries.title: Cross-server matchmaking, queue leases, and secure teleports
entries.summary: Use ephemeral queues for coordination, durable state for economic data, and recover partial teleport failures.
checklist: Duplicate queue delivery cannot create duplicate assignments
Expired reservations have an explicit recovery path
Destination verifies eligibility independently of teleport metadata
entries.content:
## Assign each service one responsibility
MemoryStore holds temporary tickets, short-lived match reservations, and bounded expiry state. DataStore holds durable player progress. MessagingService can notify servers that state changed; delivery is best effort, so use a shared lookup path if missing a message would strand a player. Keep TTLs tied to the duration of the workflow. Queue reads use an invisibility lease; acknowledge with RemoveAsync after durable or safely recoverable processing. Expect redelivery after the invisibility interval if the consumer dies.

## Worked matchmaking sequence
A lobby submits a user-scoped ticket with a unique ID and cancellation generation. A matcher checks eligibility and claims a match ID before assigning a destination. Record the assignment under a short-lived key accessible by source and destination. Only then acknowledge the queue batch. Reprocessing a ticket consults the existing assignment. Because assignment and queue removal are separate operations, design duplicate paths explicitly. Use server-side TeleportAsync; cache retry state per player, handle failures thrown by the call and later TeleportInitFailed events, and do not replay already arrived players.

## Recover partial arrival
Treat teleport metadata as a lookup hint, never as proof of currency, inventory or membership. Recheck assignment and expiration server-side before admitting a player. Handle departed, cancelled, and expired tickets without kicking everyone in a match. Test a disappearing matcher, duplicated tickets, one player failing in a group teleport, a missed notification, and a reconnect. Use published staging for production-equivalent behavior, check current supported Studio teleport modes, and do not use live player data for failure drills.

entries.title: Inventory, quest progress, and idempotent rewards
entries.summary: Model grants and quest claims as server-owned state transitions with stable IDs and atomic rewards.
checklist: Claims are idempotent across a retry
Progress comes from authoritative gameplay events
A full inventory cannot leave a partially applied reward
entries.content:
## Model grants and claims
Use stable item and quest IDs with versioned server-owned definitions. Store item stacks separately from unique item instances, with explicit capacity and ownership checks. A quest has an active phase, progress, claimable status and a claim record. The client projects this state; it requests Claim(questId) and never supplies counts or reward values.

## Commit reward and claim together
On an authoritative gameplay event, update progress monotonically where appropriate and suppress duplicates using a stable event ID or a domain invariant. A claim operation resolves the quest definition, rechecks progress and capacity, mutates inventory or wallet, and records a stable claim key in the same profile transition. For repeatable quests include the server-assigned cycle ID. If capacity is unavailable, leave the claim available or use a documented overflow destination. Never mark success before the reward transition is committed.

## Test lifecycle changes
Test completing progress while UI is closed, two requests for the same claim, reconnect during an ambiguous save, a rotation while another player is finishing the old cycle, and full capacity. Verify server state after every case. For multi-profile trades, a one-key write cannot atomically debit both profiles; use a recoverable transaction protocol or keep trading disabled until such a system exists.

entries.title: Match state machines, checkpoints, and respawns
entries.summary: Make legal match transitions explicit and keep progress and spawn decisions on the server.
checklist: Duplicate touches and timers cannot advance twice
Late joins and simultaneous respawns are covered
Round teardown clears all old connections

sources.title: Network ownership, movement validation, and physics

entries.content:
## Give the match a lifecycle
Use a server-owned sequence such as Lobby → Starting → Active → Results → Reset. One controller owns transitions and records a round ID, generation and deadline. UI renders deadlines from a synchronized presentation clock, while server time determines actual phase changes. After a yield or delayed callback, check the generation before committing. Decide early whether a late join spectates, waits, or takes a slot; keep this separate from character death.

## Save verified checkpoint progress
Register anchored markers with stable ordered IDs. Resolve a touch candidate to an active character and player, verify current round and sequence, and consume each checkpoint once. A client-owned character can move in unexpected ways; in a competitive obby add server checks appropriate to the permitted movement and never grant major rewards merely from a touch. On CharacterAdded, use the latest valid server record to choose an eligible spawn and run character-bound work under its own scope. Keep temporary progress in round state; only write durable progression if that is part of the design.

## Test transitions
Exercise simultaneous touches from multiple character parts, out-of-order markers, death at the phase boundary, spam respawn, and a player leaving just before rewards. Assert each round settles once, a previous round cannot fire a delayed payout, and a late join sees the current phase immediately.

entries.title: Developer product receipts and durable purchase grants
entries.summary: Grant repeatable developer products through one server receipt handler with an atomic, idempotent profile update.
checklist: Repeated PurchaseId grants only once across servers
Persisted receipt and reward are written together
Unknown products and transient failures are surfaced for recovery
entries.content:
## ProcessReceipt and PurchaseId routing
In a ProcessReceipt-based experience, register one callback in server code. Route ProductId through a server-owned catalog containing supported historical IDs; PurchaseId identifies the transaction, and PlayerId identifies the buyer. PromptProductPurchaseFinished is a presentation signal and does not authorize a grant. Defer unavailable profiles, transient storage failures, or unknown products with NotProcessedYet and bounded operational alerts; do not discard a paid entitlement because configuration was missing.

## BindReceiptHandler routing and retry behavior
Roblox also documents BindReceiptHandler for DeveloperProduct receipts. A matching bound handler takes precedence over ProcessReceipt; unmatched receipts can fall through to ProcessReceipt. A bound handler returns ReceiptDecision.Processed or ReceiptDecision.NotProcessedYet, while ProcessReceipt returns ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted or ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet. Keep both routes on the same durable grant adapter during migration and verify filtered, catch-all and fallback routing with staging products. Do not depend on a timed retry from ProcessReceipt: Roblox documents retries on later qualifying purchases or rejoin, not a timer. Alert on unresolved events so support can investigate gaps.

## Write the reward and receipt as one durable decision
Under the authoritative profile writer, inspect the persisted PurchaseId. If already granted, acknowledge without adding currency. Otherwise write the new wallet value and receipt marker together on the same profile key with UpdateAsync. Return PurchaseGranted only after confirmed durable success or a confirmed previously applied receipt. Keep the transform deterministic and non-yielding. Do not emit analytics or change external instances in that callback. Avoid a separate receipt ledger and wallet write without a reconciliation protocol: a crash between them can lose or duplicate the reward. Plan receipt history capacity and recovery before shipping at scale; arbitrary eviction can invalidate deduplication.

## Pure receipt transform example
The storage adapter calls this shape inside an ownership-checked UpdateAsync transform. The adapter validates the loaded record, product mapping and balance bounds before invoking it. This illustration covers one currency and omits storage and receipt acknowledgement.

```luau
--!strict
type Profile = { coins: number, receipts: {[string]: boolean} }

local function grantCoins(current: Profile, purchaseId: string, amount: number): Profile
    if current.receipts[purchaseId] then
        return current
    end

    local nextProfile = table.clone(current)
    nextProfile.receipts = table.clone(current.receipts)
    nextProfile.coins += amount
    nextProfile.receipts[purchaseId] = true
    return nextProfile
end

local base: Profile = { coins = 10, receipts = {} }
local granted = grantCoins(base, "purchase-001", 50)
assert(base.coins == 10 and not base.receipts["purchase-001"])
assert(granted.coins == 60)
assert(grantCoins(granted, "purchase-001", 50).coins == 60)
```

## Review a crash matrix
Run isolated tests for first delivery, same PurchaseId twice, same ProductId with two PurchaseIds, concurrent delivery to two servers, an unknown ID, a failed write, and a crash after commit but before acknowledgement. The last case must acknowledge the existing grant on redelivery. If regular profile saves cache player state, merge or refresh it at the same mutation boundary, so a later save cannot erase the committed grant. Emit best-effort observability after commit and distinguish business-level grant deduplication from analytics delivery.

entries.title: Passes, subscriptions, and policy-aware shop entitlements
entries.summary: Separate permanent pass ownership, recurring subscription state, and consumable developer-product receipts.
checklist: Server checks product ownership before granting access
Restricted offers are also blocked by the backend
The UI distinguishes unknown state from a definitive denial
entries.content:
## Choose the correct product type
Use a pass for a one-time durable privilege and query ownership with UserOwnsGamePassAsync on the server at relevant entry points. Subscriptions have changing entitlement status; verify current subscription state using the documented API and recheck on lifecycle changes. A repeatable currency pack is a developer product and belongs in the receipt pipeline. Keep an entitlement adapter separate from pricing and rendering. Explicitly model unknown provider state; when verification fails, offer a retry and avoid granting restricted benefits without confirmation.

## Make the shop policy-aware
Use PolicyService information for current eligibility when relevant. Enforce decisions in the server action as well as the offer display, including restrictions on paid random items and trading. If the experience offers randomness in scope of Roblox's policy, present actual numerical odds and the full outcome set before payment, and account for modifiers in the odds shown. Prefer a deterministic alternative when eligibility cannot be verified. Confirm current policy and product availability before release.

## Test without conflating UI and ownership
Test returning owners, a completed or cancelled prompt, subscription renewal and expiration, service failure, policy changes, and repeated requests. Use clearly labeled staging products; do not depend on cached UI labels to authorize access. Keep receipt grants and entitlement rechecks independently observable.

entries.title: UI controllers, optimistic updates, and stale response handling
entries.summary: Separate authoritative state from transient interaction state and handle delayed responses without lying to the player.
checklist: Responses from old views cannot update active screens
Mutations announce pending and failure states
Respawn and screen reopen release subscriptions
entries.content:
## Keep a presentation model
A shop screen can keep loading, ready, empty and error states separately from selection, pending purchase and focus. Subscribe to inventory and wallet projections rather than making every button fetch the server. Derive price formatting, labels and disabled states in one presenter so mouse, touch and controller paths behave consistently. Keep entitlement checks on the server while matching policy-aware UI.

## Reconcile delayed and failed requests
An action captures a screen generation and request ID. Disable duplicate submissions while pending or reuse the same operation ID. If the player closes the view and opens another, ignore a completion that belongs to the previous generation, but let the shared data model reconcile any real update. Display reversible local feedback optimistically; avoid optimistic ownership, permanent rewards or confirmed purchases. When a request times out, show uncertain state and refresh authority instead of blindly assuming failure.

## Exercise the race matrix
Give the fake adapter manually resolvable requests. Open A, close it, open B, then resolve A after B and verify the view remains B. Test response reordering, cancellation before submit, failure with retry, and gamepad focus after refreshing a list. In Studio, verify re-entry after respawn and repeated open/close cycles without duplicate connections.

entries.title: Server-validated gameplay combat and ability state
entries.summary: Keep combat outcomes authoritative while allowing responsive local effects and fair corrections.
checklist: Hit and damage changes are decided on the server
Ability phases and costs settle once for each action ID
Multi-client tests cover delay and obstructed targets

sources.title: Network ownership, movement validation, and physics

entries.content:
## Split game outcomes from presentation
The client can render a windup or a local trace immediately, but sends a bounded action intent. The server checks equipped ability, living state, cooldown, origin, range, target, teams and obstruction as appropriate. Derive damage from server definitions. With Workspace:Raycast, filter the attacker's character and choose collision groups matching actual combat rules. A client animation marker can trigger presentation; it cannot grant a hit. Add a unique action ID to match predicted visuals to confirmed or rejected outcomes.

## Keep latency compensation bounded
Start with a server check and observe real client latency before adding rewind. If a competitive experience requires historical validation, keep a short server-owned history and use constrained server timing. Reject unknown or invalid timestamps rather than trusting the client clock or granting arbitrary rewind. Record correction rates and compare outcomes across latency bands. Keep the core ability phases and resource commits explicit even if movement prediction changes.

## Exercise edge cases
Test obstructed targets, targets leaving before confirmation, simultaneous attacks, player death in the windup, duplicate action IDs, delayed packets, and ownership transitions on moving objects. Verify no duplicate resource deduction or damage and that prediction can be corrected without leaving stuck effects.

entries.title: Parallel Luau Actors and bounded work scheduling
entries.summary: Split measured CPU-heavy work into independent units and preserve safe serial publication.
checklist: Each parallel API used is safe in its documented context
Stale results are discarded using generation IDs
Parallel version improves measured tails on target hardware
entries.content:
## Decide if parallel work fits
Start with a measured CPU hotspot and an independent workload such as spatial sampling or pure per-entity decisions. Parallel Luau runs work under Actors; requiring a ModuleScript in different Actor VMs can create separate module state. Require modules before entering parallel execution. Use partitions of sensible size, since per-item messaging and coordination can dominate small jobs.

## Snapshot, compute, publish
Capture inputs and a generation or tick ID, distribute bounded work, and merge results through a serial owner. Use Actor messages or deliberate shared structures where appropriate; don't assume writable ordinary tables are shared. Check API thread-safety when calling engine methods. Return to serial context before writing Instances that do not support parallel mutation. When a result returns for a removed entity, skip it. Bound how much work can be outstanding so late batches cannot overwhelm the next frame.

## Test allocation and worst case
Compare an equivalent serial implementation under typical and peak population. Track frame-time tails and scheduling overhead, not just aggregate throughput. Test empty partitions, skewed work, level reset while work is in flight, and map teardown. If there is no useful gain, keep serial batching; it is simpler to recover and inspect.

entries.title: Reproducible Roblox debugging and production observability
entries.summary: Find the first broken invariant, link observations across server and client, and diagnose failures without exposing sensitive data.
checklist: Reproduction includes place version, role and input conditions
Server and client logs share a correlation ID
A regression test observes the original broken invariant
entries.content:
## Establish a controlled reproduction
Capture initial state, action, expected behavior and actual behavior. State the place or package version, whether the failure is on client or server, and whether it requires reconnect, latency, a streamed zone, or a specific device. Reduce the scenario until it still fails. Set a conditional breakpoint at the earliest unexpected state, then inspect call stack, locals and watches; switch simulation context when the same action crosses a remote.

## Instrument the boundaries
Log one structured event at ingress, durable commit and terminal failure with operation ID, subsystem, revision or phase, and a bounded reason code. Pair client request IDs with server-side outcomes where possible. Never log raw credentials, user-created text, or full unbounded payloads. Rate-limit recurring logs and preserve high-level error counters; use durations and sample reconnect incidents. Distinguish timeout, rejection and committed-with-lost-response so retry decisions are safe.

## Verify and prevent recurrence
Run the same reproduction on the fix. Compare state before and after, not only console silence. Keep a minimal regression fixture for the broken invariant and add a measurable alert if the failure class matters in production. Record recovery steps and when replay is safe. For a memory leak, measure repeated character or view cycles and compare retained objects after idle, not a one-time heap reading.

entries.title: External HTTP integrations, secrets, and durable retries
entries.summary: Keep external dependencies off the gameplay hot path and make outbound operations safe to retry.
checklist: Only predetermined hosts and operations are supported
Credentials and provider errors are redacted
Retrying a write cannot duplicate an external side effect
entries.content:
## Narrow the adapter
Put HTTP access in server-only code. Use fixed HTTPS service endpoints and a predefined operation map; player input must not decide the destination URL or headers. Use Roblox's documented secret store and the minimum credentials needed. Validate request payload bounds, protect requests with pcall, inspect RequestAsync response status, and validate decoded response shape. Keep tokens and raw upstream bodies out of logs and client messages.

## Isolate dependency failure
For a live leaderboard decoration, prefer stale cached information or graceful unavailability to blocking match start. Bound outstanding calls and retries, use backoff with jitter, and separate transient status from permanent validation failures. For a durable outbound write, use a stable operation ID accepted by the destination and keep a recoverable pending record. If the remote may have committed before timing out, reconcile using its operation lookup before repeating an unkeyed write.

## Fault-inject at the boundary
Inject a fake transport that yields, rejects with a throttle, returns malformed JSON, and commits then times out. Verify degradation, bounded worker concurrency, and that recovery does not double-charge or double-notify. In staging, confirm allowlisted destinations and rotate the secret without exposing it in diagnostics.

entries.title: Cross-platform action bindings, modal context, and camera control
entries.summary: Bind gameplay actions to intent across devices and restore input and camera state after transitions.
checklist: Touch and controller perform the same named action
Opening a modal does not trigger gameplay actions
Death exits custom camera and input contexts
entries.content:
## Define actions by player intent
Map Interact, Confirm and Cancel to bindings appropriate to keyboard, touch and controller. Contexts distinguish gameplay, menus, vehicles and spectator states. Enter and exit contexts predictably; choose whether a modal consumes an action before it can reach gameplay. Player preference can change during a session, so update visual prompts when preferred input changes. Respect platform-reserved controls and avoid cloning responsibilities already handled by Roblox defaults.

## Pair overrides with teardown
A cinematic may switch the local camera type and enable a skip action. Capture ownership and the intended restoration behavior, then restore control on finish, respawn, screen closure, or cancellation. A stale animation or camera callback should not take control back after the new generation starts. Send only high-level intent over the network; the server decides consequential outcomes.

## Exercise mixed input in Studio and on device
Open a modal using touch, switch to a gamepad, close it, and confirm that gameplay focus returns. Test a respawn during a cinematic and rapid transitions between vehicle and normal movement. Check that buttons remain reachable on safe-area layouts and action hints match the input actually being used.

entries.title: Scalable world art, lighting, VFX, and audio budgets
entries.summary: Establish a representative scene budget and reduce expensive effects without losing gameplay cues.
checklist: Peak encounters are included in the art budget
Quality modes preserve essential cues
Performance comparisons use the same camera traversal
entries.content:
## Set a representative content budget
Choose a camera route through the densest area, include peak player effects and NPC count, and measure target hardware. Distinguish render cost, simulation cost, memory, and network replication. Limit overlapping transparent particles or repeated dynamic lights by distance and quality; fewer expensive effects are better than arbitrary blanket reductions. Reuse materials and meshes where appropriate and keep visual-only hit sparks, debris and audio client-side after an authoritative trigger.

## Preserve readability in graceful degradation
Important cues should remain distinguishable without bloom, high particle counts or sound alone. Keep collision simpler than art where appropriate and separate effect lifetime from game state. Cull or stop offscreen work where it contributes no player value. Audit ownership and collision choices after replacing props. Use streaming judiciously for world size; excessive persistence can defeat expected savings.

## Reproduce a worst-case frame
Compare cold join and traversal of the same route on a representative mobile device. Trigger combat or VFX at the busiest point. Capture frame timing and memory before and after changing one class of effect, and retain screenshots or video evidence only where hardware testing is available. Confirm performance improvement did not hide an interaction marker or accessibility cue.

entries.title: Roblox source control, place sync, packages, and CI
entries.summary: Make versioned source and place ownership unambiguous and use staged validation before publishing.
checklist: Each synced subtree has one declared owner
CI checks code and build artifacts without production credentials
Generated output is tested in staging before publish
entries.content:
## Declare the source of truth
For a repository using Rojo, designate owned subtrees and keep the project mapping in version control. Review its merge behavior and use servePlaceIds to restrict the eligible place IDs where appropriate; directories represented by source and Studio-only Instances need explicit ownership boundaries. Keep private server config out of replicated source and treat generic asset permissions separately from source mapping. Pin tool and dependency versions, inspect module source when adding third-party code, and review the generated tree before moving a module across client/server boundaries.

## Validate incrementally
CI can run formatter, analyzer and pure Luau tests, then build a place artifact where the project supports it. On staging, check that server modules, client entrypoints, required objects and asset permissions match the manifest. Treat scene or package changes as separately reviewable, with a previous known-good place available. Publish by an authenticated, scoped release process; keep production data credentials out of checks and test fixtures.

## Recover a broken sync
If a mapping change deletes or moves unexpected Instances, stop publishing, compare the generated tree to the last known artifact, and restore untracked Studio-owned work from an appropriate place version. Reproduce the bug in a disposable copy before reconnecting sync. Check both provenance and operational ownership before reapplying the source changes.

entries.title: User-generated text safety, filtering, and chat moderation
entries.summary: Treat free-form text as untrusted and match filtering to the audience before display.
checklist: Unfiltered text never reaches other players
Filter failures withhold display and give a retry path
Tests cover length, throttling and shared visibility
entries.content:
## Establish the audience and handling path
Use TextChatService for chat. For user-entered non-chat content like signs, approve a server-side path with TextService filtering and select the result method appropriate to the intended audience. For text displayed to everyone, use the non-chat broadcast result. Do not cache one recipient's result and send it as if it were appropriate for everyone. Validate length and rate limits before invoking the filter, and withhold display if the filter call fails rather than falling back to raw text.

## Control what leaves the server
Never let clients replicate user-entered labels unchecked. Avoid logging raw text or sending it to analytics. If designs allow edits or deletion of a sign, authorize the actor against the sign's server-owned identity. Never substitute manual keyword lists for platform filtering. Review current platform rules for chat, text permissions and persistent user-generated content before publishing.

## Exercise error and visibility cases
Test an empty or oversized string, a repeated submission, filter unavailability, another user trying to edit the sign, and a player joining after approved text is displayed. In each case verify other viewers see only a valid filtered projection or an appropriate placeholder.

entries.title: Deterministic Luau tests for state machines and service adapters
entries.summary: Make pure gameplay and persistence decisions executable outside Studio, then verify engine integration in Studio.
checklist: Pure tests do not wait for time or platform services
Test doubles can model an ambiguous commit
Engine interactions receive a separate multiplayer check
entries.content:
## Inject boundary values and assert invariants
Keep game rules independent from Players, DataStoreService and live clocks. For a reward cap, pass the current balance, payout and cap as validated integers. Tests should assert conservation or monotonicity in addition to a few examples. For delayed actions inject a clock function or pass now explicitly. Use a scripted fake service to model failure before commit, success, and commit followed by missing response.

## Minimal table-driven example
```luau
--!strict
local function credit(balance: number, amount: number, cap: number): number
    return math.min(balance + amount, cap)
end

local cases = {
    { initial = 0, amount = 3, expected = 3 },
    { initial = 8, amount = 5, expected = 10 },
    { initial = 10, amount = 0, expected = 10 },
}
for _, case in ipairs(cases) do
    assert(credit(case.initial, case.amount, 10) == case.expected)
end
```
This function assumes the boundary already checked nonnegative integer inputs and balance no greater than cap. Test boundary rejects separately rather than silently normalizing invalid economic data.

## Verify engine integration separately
Use Studio to check Instance lifetime, replication, input focus, physics and actual service behavior in a safe environment. Make failure diagnostics include the case name and observed state. Keep fixture data local and synthetic. A pure test proves a transition; it does not demonstrate multiplayer replication or a live purchase.
